items.headline: Small-molecule switches put therapeutic CRISPR editing under on-demand control in living tissues
items.preview: Researchers developed dual small-molecule-controlled genome editing systems for CRISPR.
items.article:
In a study published in Science Translational Medicine, a team of researchers led by Dr. Wang Yu from the Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology of the Chinese Academy of Sciences developed PRINCE and Little Prince, dual small-molecule-controlled genome editing systems that allow CRISPR activity to be switched on by drug inducers and kept largely silent in their absence.
Why this matters: This advancement aims to enhance the efficiency and controllability of therapeutic genome editing, reducing off-target effects and improving safety for potential clinical applications.

items.headline: Novartis’ strategy in 2026: rebuilding the pipeline after Entresto
items.preview: Novartis focuses on innovative medicines while facing challenges from patent expiries.
items.article:
Novartis is concentrating on four core therapeutic areas: cardiovascular, renal and metabolic diseases, oncology, immunology, and neuroscience, supported by technology platforms including xRNA and gene therapy. Despite a significant decline in sales from older products like Entresto due to generic competition, Novartis is investing heavily to strengthen its pipeline through acquisitions and new therapies.
Why this matters: This strategic shift is crucial for Novartis to maintain its market position and continue delivering innovative treatments amidst increasing competition and patent expirations.

items.headline: Is Stem Cell Longevity Therapy in Mexico a Viable Option for Canadian Patients?
items.preview: Stem cell therapy in Mexico offers Canadians advanced anti-aging treatments not available at home.
items.article:
For Canadians seeking advanced anti-aging treatments, stem cell longevity therapy in Mexico provides access to high-dose mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) infusions not readily available domestically. These treatments, regulated by COFEPRIS, focus on reducing systemic inflammation and promoting tissue regeneration.
Why this matters: As Canadian regulations limit access to such therapies, this option presents a viable alternative for patients looking to enhance their health and longevity through regenerative medicine.

items.headline: CHO, HeLa and HEK293: Comparing key cell lines for drug discovery and biologic development
items.preview: A comparison of CHO, HeLa, and HEK293 cell lines highlights their roles in biopharmaceuticals.
items.article:
Mammalian cell lines are crucial in the production of recombinant therapeutic proteins, vaccines, and other clinically relevant drugs. CHO cells are the gold standard for biologics production, while HeLa cells are essential for cancer research and HEK293 cells are pivotal in gene therapy development.
Why this matters: Understanding the strengths and weaknesses of these cell lines can guide researchers in selecting the appropriate models for drug discovery and development, ultimately impacting therapeutic outcomes.

items.headline: The cell cloud: Adopting systems biology concepts in the era of single-cell immunology
items.preview: A new model proposes viewing cellular identities as probabilistic distributions rather than discrete types.
items.article:
The advent of single-cell RNA sequencing has revealed a continuous landscape of cellular identities, challenging the traditional view of discrete cell types. This 'cell cloud' model emphasizes the probabilistic nature of cellular states and suggests that immunotherapies should target the entire distribution of cell states rather than fixed populations.
Why this matters: This approach could enhance the effectiveness of immunotherapies by acknowledging the dynamic and complex nature of immune cell identities, leading to more personalized treatment strategies.
